title: Compatible root rotations give the full profinite torsor comparison
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $H$ be a nonzero commutative ring of characteristic $p$, let $I$ be a finite set and $t_i\in H$ for $i\in I$. Suppose there are primitive roots $\zeta_n\in H$ for all positive integers $n$ prime to $p$, satisfying $\zeta_m^{m/n}=\zeta_n$ for $n\mid m$, and with $\zeta_n^a-\zeta_n^b$ a unit whenever $a,b$ are distinct residues modulo $n$. Put $f=\prod_i t_i$ (empty product $1$), $J=(t_i)_i$, $H_n=H[x_i]_{i\in I}/(x_i^n-t_i)_i$ and $H_\infty=\varinjlim_{(n,p)=1}H_n$, with transitions $x_{i,n}\mapsto x_{i,m}^{m/n}$. Write $U^\circ=\operatorname{Spec}H[1/f]$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}H_\infty$ and $T^\circ=\operatorname{Spec}H_\infty[1/f]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-sfb-full-parameter-root-tower]. Let $G=(\prod_{q\ne p}\mathbf Z_q)^I$, with $q$ over primes and its profinite product topology, and let $G_n=(\mathbf Z/n)^I$.
Root rotations $x_{i,n}\mapsto\zeta_n^{a_i}x_{i,n}$ define compatible actions of $G_n$ on $\operatorname{Spec}H_n$. There is a topological group identification $G\cong\varprojlim_{(n,p)=1}G_n$ with the ordinary residue projections. For $T_n^\circ=\operatorname{Spec}H_n[1/f]$, the actual comparisons
$$T_n^\circ[G_n]\xrightarrow{\sim}T_n^\circ\times_{U^\circ}T_n^\circ,\quad(x,a)\mapsto(x,\zeta_n^a x),$$
are scheme isomorphisms, commute with power transitions, and induce the scheme isomorphism
$$T^\circ[G]\xrightarrow{\sim}T^\circ\times_{U^\circ}T^\circ,\quad(x,g)\mapsto(x,gx).$$
Here $X[P]$ denotes the inverse limit of finite disjoint unions [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects], and fibre products are [def-pc-fibre-product]. The quotient map sending every root to zero defines $i:\operatorname{Spec}(H/J)\to T$, fixed by all root rotations. All these maps commute with ring homomorphisms preserving the parameters and compatible roots. For $I=\varnothing$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}H$, $G=1$ and $i$ is the identity. Empty punctured loci are allowed; no existence of residual charts or lisse extension of an initially given sheaf is asserted.

proof.text: For each tame $n$, define the $H$-algebra automorphism $r_{n,a}$ on the quotient generators by $x_{i,n}\mapsto\zeta_n^{a_i}x_{i,n}$. It preserves the relations because $(\zeta_n^{a_i}x_{i,n})^n=t_i$, is independent of residue representatives, and has inverse $r_{n,-a}$. Composition adds labels. If $n\mid m$, then $(\zeta_m^{a_i}x_{i,m})^{m/n}=\zeta_n^{a_i}x_{i,m}^{m/n}$, so reduction of labels intertwines the power transitions. The quotient and colimit presentations in [def-sfb-full-parameter-root-tower] therefore give the stated compatible actions on every finite spectrum and on $T$. Contravariance causes no order ambiguity because the label groups are abelian.

proof.text: Write $N_p=\{n>0:(n,p)=1\}$ and $L=\varprojlim_{n\in N_p}\mathbf Z/n$, with residue transitions and the subspace topology from the product of discrete rings. For $(z_q)_{q\ne p}$, CRT [lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product], applied to the prime-power ideals of $\mathbf Z$, gives the unique $a_n\in\mathbf Z/n$ whose residue at $q^{v_q(n)}$ is $\rho_{v_q(n)}(z_q)$. The compatibility in [lem-exc-padic-residue-universal-property] and CRT uniqueness imply $a_m\bmod n=a_n$ for $n\mid m$. Conversely the projections $L\to\mathbf Z/q^b$ form compatible ring homomorphisms; that same residue universal property supplies a unique $L\to\mathbf Z_q$. CRT uniqueness and separation by all $\rho_b$ show these two constructions are inverse ring homomorphisms. Every forward coordinate depends on finitely many continuous residue maps: each residue fibre is a coset of $q^b\mathbf Z_q$, open by the norm criterion in the residue node (a sufficiently small norm ball is contained in it). For the inverse, equality of the $q^b$ coordinates bounds the norm of the difference by $q^{-b}$, which proves continuity into each $\mathbf Z_q$. This gives the required topological group identification after taking the finite product over $I$, with precisely the ordinary residue projections; $n=1$ uses the singleton residue ring.

proof.text: Put $A=H[1/f]$ and $B_n=H_n[1/f]$. The universal property of localization gives $\varinjlim_n B_n=H_\infty[1/f]$: a compatible family of maps $H_n[1/f]\to C$ is exactly a compatible family $H_n\to C$ whose common image of $f$ is invertible, hence exactly a map $H_\infty[1/f]\to C$. The directed index $N_p$ is nonempty and multiplication supplies upper bounds. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit] identifies its scheme limit $\varprojlim_n T_n^\circ$ canonically with $T^\circ$, preserving the root coordinates and projections. No injectivity of ring transitions or nonemptiness of the puncture is needed.

Choose an enumeration $I\simeq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ and apply [lem-sfb-compatible-kummer-tower-cech] to $H$ and these $r$ parameters. Its hypotheses are exactly the primitive-root compatibility and unit-difference hypotheses here; it allows arbitrary characteristic-$p$ rings and $r=0$. Its displayed finite comparisons are the maps $(x,a)\mapsto(x,\zeta_n^a x)$, and its transition clause is for the same power maps and residue reductions as above. Its infinite comparison, with the topological identification of step 2 and the canonical scheme limit of step 3, is precisely $T^\circ[G]\simeq T^\circ\times_{U^\circ}T^\circ$. The notation $X[P]$ agrees with [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects]. Relabelling the parameters changes none of the formulas, since every generator retains its own label.

proof.text: Let $q:H\to H/J$ be the quotient homomorphism. At every $n$, the assignment $h\mapsto q(h)$ and $x_{i,n}\mapsto0$ respects $x_{i,n}^n=t_i$, since $n>0$ and $q(t_i)=0$. These homomorphisms $H_n\to H/J$ are compatible: $0^{m/n}=0$ for $n\mid m$, because $m/n>0$. The colimit presentation [def-sfb-full-parameter-root-tower] yields a homomorphism $e:H_\infty\to H/J$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] its spectrum is $i:\operatorname{Spec}(H/J)\to T$. For each rotation, $e(r_{n,a}(x_{i,n}))=q(\zeta_n^{a_i})\,0=0=e(x_{i,n})$, and constants are fixed. Equality on generators at every stage gives $e\circ r_g=e$, hence $g\circ i=i$.

proof.text: For a ring map $\phi:H\to H^\prime$ preserving the listed data, define $H_n\to H_n^\prime$ by $h\mapsto\phi(h)$ and $x_{i,n}\mapsto x_{i,n}^\prime$. The relations and power transitions agree term by term; moreover $\phi(\zeta_n^{a_i})x_{i,n}^\prime=(\zeta_n^\prime)^{a_i}x_{i,n}^\prime$, so these maps commute with rotations, then with the induced colimit maps and localizations. The comparison naturality is the base-change clause of [lem-sfb-compatible-kummer-tower-cech]. Since $\phi(J)\subseteq J^\prime$, the induced quotient map sends $q(h)$ to $q^\prime(\phi(h))$; the two composites $H_\infty\to H^\prime/J^\prime$ agree on constants and send every root to zero. This proves naturality of $i$ too. Step 2 depends only on $p,I$ and is unchanged by $\phi$.

proof.text: If $I=\varnothing$, every $H_n=H$ and every transition is the identity, while $f=1$ and $J=0$. Thus $H_\infty=H$, $G=1$, $e$ is the identity, and all comparisons reduce to the identity comparison. If the puncture is empty, the comparison node already allows its zero localization rings; none of steps 1 or 5 localizes at $f$, so the fixed boundary map still exists. These constructions give only the maps claimed in the statement.

lean.statement: theorem fullRootRotationTorsor (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) {I H : Type u} [Fintype I] [CommRing H] [Nontrivial H] [CharP H p] (t : I → H) (ζ : TameRootOrder p → H) (hζ : ∀ n, IsPrimitiveRoot (ζ n) n.val) (hcompat : ∀ (n m : TameRootOrder p), n.val ∣ m.val → ζ m ^ (m.val / n.val) = ζ n) (hunit : ∀ (n : TameRootOrder p) (a b : ZMod n.val), a ≠ b → IsUnit (ζ n ^ a.val - ζ n ^ b.val)) : ∃ D : FullRootRotationData p t ζ, ∀ (K : Type u) [CommRing K] [Nontrivial K] [CharP K p] (s : I → K) (η : TameRootOrder p → K) (_hη : ∀ n, IsPrimitiveRoot (η n) n.val) (_hcompat : ∀ (n m : TameRootOrder p), n.val ∣ m.val → η m ^ (m.val / n.val) = η n) (_hunit : ∀ (n : TameRootOrder p) (a b : ZMod n.val), a ≠ b → IsUnit (η n ^ a.val - η n ^ b.val)) (φ : H →+* K) (_ht : ∀ i, φ (t i) = s i) (_hroots : ∀ n, φ (ζ n) = η n) (E : FullRootRotationData p s η), Nonempty (FullRootRotationBaseChange D E φ)
